one_liner: Rust Rego interpreter (OPA's policy language), embeddable from C/C++; about 10x faster than an opa eval CLI run on one ACI policy.
what_it_does: Evaluates Open Policy Agent Rego policies in-process: create an Engine, add .rego policies and JSON/YAML data, set input, then call eval_rule (returns a Value) or eval_query (returns OPA-format JSON results). It is a library plus an example CLI ('regorus eval' mirrors 'opa eval'), not a replacement for the OPA server. C and C++ use it through a cbindgen-generated FFI (bindings/cpp/regorus.hpp, CMake via Corrosion); C#, Go, Java, Python, Ruby and WASM bindings exist but are not published to package registries.
how_it_is_fast: Native Rust evaluator with no Go runtime or garbage collector to start, so short-lived evaluations avoid OPA's process and compiler start-up cost; a comment in examples/regorus/main.rs says eval_rule skips query parsing and is faster than eval_query. Newer releases add RVM, a register-based bytecode VM with fixed-width 32-bit instructions, pooled per-frame register windows, load-time-resolved literal and builtin tables and rule caching (docs/rvm/architecture.md). LRU caches hold compiled regex and glob patterns across evaluations (cache feature), and features can be compiled out to shrink the binary (6.3 MB default, 1.9 MB with no default features).
when_to_use: Evaluating Rego authorization or admission policies inside a C, C++ or Rust process where running OPA as a sidecar or linking a Go runtime is unwanted.
Short-lived or per-request policy checks where OPA CLI or Go start-up dominates (the README's ACI example: 4.6 ms vs 45.2 ms per whole-process run).
Constrained or confidential-computing targets: no_std builds (opa-no-std feature), a freestanding C binding without libc, WASM, and feature flags to strip unneeded builtins.
Projects that want a memory-safe evaluator: the library sets forbid(unsafe_code) outside Verus verification builds.
when_not_to_use: Policies that rely on builtins Regorus lacks: JWT and other cryptographic builtins (unsupported by design), net.cidr_* functions, graphql, providers.aws, rego.parse_module, rego.metadata.*, strings.render_template and some glob cases (README OPA Conformance list).
When you need the OPA server feature set (REST API, bundle service, decision logs); the README documents only a library and an example CLI.

Long-running services that compile a policy once and evaluate many times: the published 10x includes OPA process start-up and compilation, and no in-process comparison against OPA's Go API or 'opa bench' is published.
If you need ready-made packages for Go, Python, Java or .NET: the README says bindings are not published and must be built yourself.

integration.form: crate (Rust); static or shared library for C/C++ via the cbindgen FFI crate built with Corrosion
integration.dependencies: Core: anyhow, serde, serde_json, lazy_static, thiserror, num-bigint, num-traits, spin and vstd (Verus std, pinned to a dated pre-release); the default full-opa feature adds regex, globset, chrono/chrono-tz, jsonschema, url, uuid, semver, yaml_serde, lru, parking_lot, data-encoding and ipnet.
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 2021 edition, no rust-version declared on crates.io; C++ binding needs C++17 and CMake 3.12+ (Corrosion fetched by FetchContent).
integration.platforms: Any Rust target; no_std and WASM builds; CI cross-compiles musl targets (xtask test-musl).
integration.thread_safety: Engine is a mutable single-owner object; the C++ wrapper exposes Engine::clone() for per-thread copies. With the default arc feature values use Arc and extensions must be Send + Sync. Concurrency guarantees beyond that are not documented.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same Rego semantics and the same JSON result format as opa eval (README shows a diff of the two outputs), but missing builtins, a library API instead of OPA's server and Go API, and a CLI default of strict builtin errors where OPA is non-strict.

gotchas: The README Performance commands are stale: tests/aci/framework.rego is Rego v0 syntax (rule bodies without 'if'), the regorus CLI now defaults to Rego v1 (the parser bails with "`if` keyword is required before rule body") and OPA 1.x also defaults to v1. Rerun verbatim with current versions, both commands probably time a parse error; add --v0 to regorus and --v0-compatible to OPA. The published numbers were already in the README by January 2024 (commit aabf329), when both tools defaulted to v0.

The benchmark times two whole CLI processes, including file loading, parsing and compiling a 54 KB policy and Go runtime start-up for OPA (OPA user time 68.8 ms exceeds its 45.2 ms wall time). The in-repo Criterion bench (benches/aci_benchmark.rs) times only regorus eval_rule, so no evaluation-only ratio against OPA exists.
The regorus CLI turns strict builtin errors on unless --non-strict is passed ('default behavior of OPA'), so builtin errors that OPA treats as undefined are raised as errors.
Cargo.toml and crates.io list the licence as 'MIT AND Apache-2.0 AND BSD-3-Clause', not plain MIT; check the bundled-code notices before vendoring.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No sibling interprets Rego; the closest analogue is sjsonnet, another configuration-language interpreter benchmarked against its Go reference implementation. Pick Regorus when the job is evaluating OPA/Rego policies in-process from C++ or Rust without a Go runtime; the general-purpose interpreters in this category (LuaJIT, PyPy, Wren) do not apply.
verified_claims_summary: First-party hyperfine runs in the README: 'regorus eval' on the Azure Container Instances policy (tests/aci, query data.framework.mount_overlay=x) took 4.6 ms +/- 0.2 ms over 422 runs versus 45.2 ms +/- 0.6 ms over 62 runs for the same 'opa eval' command line, about 10x (derived from page data). Both are whole-process CLI timings recorded by January 2024 on unstated hardware with unstated rustc and OPA versions (the README at that commit cited conformance with OPA v0.60.0), using one policy and one query.
status_note: Active Microsoft project (crates.io 0.12.0 released 2026-09-01, last commit 2026-10-01, about 2.64 million crates.io downloads, 1.28 million recent); copyable under the triple licence above, but the README's benchmark commands need --v0 flags to reproduce today.
